items.summary: Reinforcement learning for large language models disproportionately improves easy tasks, and an adaptive sampling method called NGU reallocates compute to harder problems to boost overall performance.

items.title: Pick Your Poison: Learning to Select Poison Sets for Stronger LLM Backdoor Attacks
items.summary: Backdoor vulnerability in fine-tuned language models varies drastically with poison selection, and a learned set-scoring method improves worst-case attack success by identifying high-impact poisoned examples.

items.title: Another Blueprint In The Wall: How to Ask Frontier AI Like a Kid?
items.summary: This paper reports experiments across six frontier model types from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google DeepMind. Ten independent sessions per model type used the same three stage prompt sequence, progressing from architectural preference to a full ASCII backbone. Under the school audience framing, responses repeatedly converged on a shared architectural pattern built around persistent latent…

items.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
items.summary: Recent work extends recursive self-improvement (RSI) to agent harnesses for long-horizon coding and terminal tasks, enabling agents to improve execution mechanisms from experience. However, generalizable harness RSI remains challenging. First, evolving harnesses on evaluation benchmarks or their subsets makes it difficult to distinguish reusable improvements from benchmark-specific adaptation.…

items.title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model
items.summary: A shared trajectory model unifies goal and dynamics prediction with action generation for language-conditioned robot control, improving adaptation and success through joint denoising and test-time scaling.

items.title: MInTRL: Off-policy Intervention can boost On-policy RL
items.summary: Minimal Intervention Reinforcement Learning improves on-policy exploration by applying sparse local corrections during rollouts and training with a sequence-level advantage-regression objective.

items.title: Modality-Autoregressive World-Action Models
items.summary: World-action models (WAMs) jointly model future observations and actions, typically predicting the future as RGB images. Other visual modalities such as depth, pretrained visual features, and point tracks can more efficiently capture geometric, semantic, and motion features. However, how best to combine these modalities within WAMs remains an open question. We introduce ModAR, the first WAM to…

items.title: Mind2Dialogue: Training Human-Aware Language Models by Simulating User Mental States
items.summary: As language models become more capable, long-term collaboration in learning, reasoning, and decision-making calls for a deeper understanding of the people they serve. Yet training such human-aware language models faces a fundamental supervision gap because current datasets for LLM assistant training contain few if any well-informed responses explicitly grounded in users' unspoken beliefs and…

items.title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: ESRL improves reinforcement learning for mixture-of-experts language models by exploring expert routing with anchored high-confidence experts, entropy-adaptive perturbation, and path replay to boost rollout diversity and training performance.

items.title: Enabling Creative Exploration for Vibe Design Agents
items.summary: Separating design exploration from code generation via structured intermediate specifications enables diverse UI alternatives without altering downstream generation settings.

items.title: Disentangling Representation Evolution in Transformers through Directional Decomposition
items.summary: Transformer representations evolve through learned additive transformations that either preserve their current direction or redirect it. We study this evolution as a functional geometry, decomposing learned updates into parallel and perpendicular components. items.title: Anthropic merges Claude Chat, Cowork, and more into a single product
items.summary: Anthropic is merging Claude Chat and Cowork into a single product. Instead of users picking between interfaces, Claude now decides on its own whether a task needs a quick answer or a bigger workflow.
